target_customer: Hospitals, cardiology echo labs and ultrasound device or reporting software vendors that read heart ultrasounds
problem: Echocardiogram interpretation is variable and diseases such as cardiac amyloidosis are missed by human readers; the company packages peer reviewed AI models into the clinical workflow.
business_model: Clinical AI software licensed to health systems and imaging software partners; FDA cleared algorithms
product_category: AI diagnostics for cardiac ultrasound (medical device software)

founders.name: David Ouyang
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page. HeartLab announcement of 2025-10 names him as InVision CEO.

competitors.name: Ultromics
competitors.traction_then: Partnered with Caption Health in Nov 2021

competitors.name: Caption Health
competitors.what: AI guided ultrasound acquisition for echo

competitors.name: Us2.ai
competitors.what: Automated echo measurement, rebranded from eko.ai in 2021 after first FDA clearance

technical_complexity.rationale: Medical grade video models validated in a blinded randomized trial and requiring FDA 510(k) clearance; the models came out of years of published research.

defensibility.rationale: FDA clearances (LVEF and cardiac amyloid) and a randomized trial create regulatory and evidence barriers that rivals must also clear.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Caption Health was later acquired by GE per Ultromics blog; InVision continued independently and won FDA clearances by 2025.

market_need_then: Echo is a high volume test with reader variability, and several AI echo vendors had obtained FDA clearances by 2021, showing clinical and regulatory demand.

branding.domain_note: Uses invisionmedtech.com, not the exact short name.

identity.voice_and_tone: Clinical and evidence driven, citing Nature, Lancet Digital Health and a randomized trial

branding.brand_signature: Peer reviewed evidence and a blinded randomized trial

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself found; the name resembles unrelated InVision companies, and credibility comes from the founders' research.

outcome_analysis: InVision is active and has turned its founders' published echo research into products: Precision LVEF (FDA 510(k) K232331) and Precision Cardiac Amyloid cleared on 2025-05-21 (K243866). A distribution partnership with HeartLab for Australia and New Zealand was announced on 2025-10-13. Funding is not publicly stated, so the financial trajectory is unknown.
